record.paper_title: Open Problems in Efficient Semi-Supervised PAC Learning
record.original_question: Consider the semi-supervised PAC model for the class C of two-sided disjunctions over {0,1}^n. A hypothesis h is a pair of disjunctions (h+, h−), where only h+ is used for classification, and h is deemed compatible with the distribution D exactly when, for every example x, h+(x) = −h−(x), so the positive and negative classes are both representable by OR-functions. The open question is whether there is a computationally efficient semi-supervised learning algorithm for this class and compatibility notion that uses as few labeled examples as the compatibility-filtered search space suggests, up to polynomial factors.

evidence.quote: Two-sided disjunctions: This is a generalization of the example above where we now allow variables to be positive indicators, negative indicators, or irrelevant. Specifically, define a “two-sided disjunction” h to be a pair of disjunctions (h+, h−) where only h+ is used for classification, but h is compatible with D iff for all examples x, h+(x) = −h−(x). That is, D is such that both the positive and negative classes can be described by OR-functions.
We now instantiate this high-level question with a few specific classes and compatibility notions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix a positive integer n and consider examples in the Boolean cube X = {0,1}^n. A two-sided disjunction is a pair h = (h^+, h^-) where h^+ and h^- are each monotone disjunctions (OR-functions) over some subsets of the n variables. The classification rule associated with h uses only h^+: an example x is labeled +1 if h^+(x) = 1 and -1 otherwise. The hypothesis h is said to be compatible with a distribution D over X if, for every x in the support of D,
    h^+(x) = ¬ h^-(x),
i.e., the positive and negative classes are both representable by OR-functions on D. Let C denote the class of two-sided disjunctions over {0,1}^n equipped with this compatibility notion.

Semi-supervised PAC model. The learner is given (i) an unlabeled sample drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution D over X, and (ii) a labeled sample drawn i.i.d. from D and labeled by some unknown target h* ∈ C that is compatible with D. For parameters ε, δ ∈ (0,1), the learner must output a hypothesis whose error with respect to (D, h*) is at most ε with probability at least 1-δ. The compatibility-filtered sample complexity is the labeled-sample size required to ε-cover, in the standard PAC sense, the subclass of C consisting of those hypotheses that are compatible with D (which can in principle be estimated using the unlabeled sample).

Problem. Decide whether there exists a learning algorithm for C in the above semi-supervised PAC model that
  (a) runs in time polynomial in n, 1/ε, and 1/δ, and
  (b) uses a number of labeled examples that matches the compatibility-filtered sample complexity for C up to factors polynomial in n, 1/ε, and log(1/δ),
while using a polynomial number of unlabeled examples.
artifact.status_search_result: Balcan, Berlind, Ehrlich, and Liang (ICML 2013, "Efficient Semi-supervised and Active Learning of Disjunctions") give efficient semi-supervised and active learning algorithms for two-sided disjunctions, but only under a mild regularity/restriction on the data distribution D, and also extend to random classification noise. This resolves the open question affirmatively under a distributional assumption; we did not find a result removing all distributional assumptions, so the problem appears partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Efficient Semi-supervised and Active Learning of Disjunctions
status_evidence.snippet: We provide efficient algorithms for learning disjunctions in the semi-supervised setting under a natural regularity assumption introduced by Balcan & Blum (2005). We prove bounds on the sample complexity of our algorithms under a mild restriction on the data distribution.
status_evidence.claim: Efficient semi-supervised algorithms for (two-sided) disjunctions are obtained under a distributional regularity assumption.

status_evidence.title: Research - Christopher Berlind
status_evidence.snippet: develops efficient algorithms for learning two-sided disjunctions, allowing efficient use of unlabeled examples in both semi-supervised and active settings
status_evidence.claim: Two-sided disjunctions admit efficient semi-supervised and active learners under the stated conditions.
